teacher:
Goal: To open the lesson and name the day’s outcome.

Run it: Say the meeting date out loud and move on. Do not warm up with small talk about English.

Check: She knows which moment of 31 August this lesson prepares.

If needed: Point at the date on the screen and name the visitor.

Move on when: She has named the visitor or the date.

Goal: To obtain her own statement of the outcome, in her words.

Run it: Ask the question and wait. Take her exact words; you will reuse them in Stage 7.

Check: She names a person and a company, not a feeling.

If needed: Offer two options: who you are, or what the company sells.

Move on when: She has said what he should know.

Goal: To name the risk she will train against, in her own priority.

Run it: Read the three. Ask which one worries her most. Do not add a fourth.

Check: She chooses one and says why in one sentence.

If needed: Ask which one already happened to her in a real meeting.

Move on when: She has chosen one.

Goal: To obtain evidence of what she already produces, before any model.

Run it: Ask her to open the meeting now. Do not correct, do not help, do not finish her sentences. Note the exact words.

Check: You have a real sample: what came out, what stopped, which word blocked her.

If needed: If she freezes, say Welcome to and wait. Nothing more.

Move on when: She has produced something, however short.

Goal: To compare her version with a model she can reuse.

Run it: Read the four moves out loud, one at a time. Then ask the question. Her answer names the gap.

Check: She names one difference, not five.

If needed: Ask which of the four moves was missing from hers.

Move on when: She has named one difference.

Goal: To fix the five lines she will use in the performance.

Run it: Drill line by line. Change one element each time: the visitor, the area, the order. Never the same repetition twice.

Check: She says each line without reading it, once.

If needed: Cut to the first three lines. Four and five can be consulted.

Move on when: She has said all five at least once without reading.

Goal: To give her a way out that is not silence.

Run it: Say a fast question she cannot answer and let her choose a repair line. Do it three times, changing the question.

Check: She uses a repair line instead of stopping.

If needed: Give her the third line only — passing the question on is the easiest to produce.

Move on when: She has used a repair line at least twice without help.

Optional: Ask which one she would use with the CEO in the room.

Goal: To make the opening portable, not memorised for one person.

Run it: Three rounds, one per visitor. She keeps the four moves and changes only what the visitor needs.

Check: The four moves survive all three rounds.

If needed: Drop to two visitors and keep the third for the performance.

Move on when: She has opened for at least two visitors without losing a move.

Goal: To run the full opening once, with support, before the performance.

Run it: One full run. Interrupt only if she stops for more than five seconds, and then only with the next move.

Check: She goes from Welcome to her area without stopping.

If needed: Let her read the map. Consulting is not failure in this case.

Move on when: She has completed one full run.

Goal: To obtain the main production of the lesson, uninterrupted.

Run it: Say Begin and stay quiet until she finishes. Write down what worked and one point to improve. Do not correct now.

Check: She produced the opening from Welcome to her area.

If needed: Nothing during. Everything goes to Stage 7.

Move on when: She has finished and stopped speaking.

Goal: To give one point of feedback from what she actually said, and retask only that part.

Run it: Name what worked, using her words. Then one point. Write first version and clearer version. Ask for the corrected part only, 20 to 40 seconds.

Check: The retask is shorter than the performance and contains the correction.

If needed: Shorten the retask to a single sentence.

Move on when: She has said the corrected part once, cleanly.

Optional: Ask where in the 31 August meeting this exact part appears.

Goal: To close on what she built and point at the next lesson by what she will do in it.

Run it: Read the three lines. Do not say tomorrow — the next lesson is on 24 August.

Check: She can say what she leaves with.

If needed: Ask her to say the opening once more, from memory, as the closing act.

Move on when: She has named one thing she can now do.

Goal: To connect to lesson 1 and name today’s outcome.

Run it: Ask her to say her opening once, from lesson 1. Do not correct it — it is the warm start, not the task.

Check: She produced the opening without the map.

If needed: Give her the first two words and let her continue.

Move on when: She has said the opening once.

Goal: To obtain her own selection before she sees the deck list.

Run it: Ask the question and wait. Write down the four she picks; you will compare with the four of Stage 4.

Check: She named four, not thirteen.

If needed: Ask which one she would say first if she had only one.

Move on when: She has named at least two moments.

Goal: To name the risk of this specific content: length and scope.

Run it: Read the three. Ask which one is most likely with this visitor.

Check: She sees that the risk here is saying too much, not too little.

If needed: Say the first one out loud as a bad example, in ten seconds of dates.

Move on when: She has chosen one.

Goal: To obtain evidence before the model: what she selects and how she links.

Run it: Ask and stay quiet. Note which dates came, and whether she linked them or listed them.

Check: You have a real sample of her selection and her linking.

If needed: If she freezes, say In 1988 and wait.

Move on when: She has produced something, however short.

Goal: To show a selection that has a logic: film, representation, portfolio, expansion.

Run it: Read the four. Then ask the question. The answer you want is that each one is a step up, not just a date.

Check: She names the logic, not the dates.

If needed: Ask what changed between 1988 and 2026 in one word.

Move on when: She has named what links them.

Goal: To fix five lines she can say without reading.

Run it: Drill each line changing one element: the year, the partner, the verb. Never the same repetition twice.

Check: She says each line once without reading.

If needed: Cut to three lines: 1988, 1996 and 2026.

Move on when: She has said all five at least once.

Goal: To separate what she owns from what she forwards.

Run it: Ask the question. The right answer is the third line, not a number she is not sure of.

Check: She forwards instead of guessing a number.

If needed: Say the third line for her and ask her to repeat it.

Move on when: She has forwarded once, cleanly.

Optional: The deck says 146 employees in total — she may use it if it comes naturally.

Goal: To make the history compressible — the real risk is length.

Run it: Three rounds, shorter each time. The one-sentence version is the one she will actually use.

Check: The one-sentence version still has a beginning and a today.

If needed: Skip the one-minute round and start at thirty seconds.

Move on when: She has produced the one-sentence version.

Goal: To join the two halves of the lesson in one run, with support.

Run it: One full run. Interrupt only if she stops for more than five seconds.

Check: She moves from history to her area without a gap.

If needed: Let her read the map. Consulting is not failure here.

Move on when: She has completed one run.

Goal: To obtain the main production: history plus her role, in one turn.

Run it: Ask the question as the visitor would and stay quiet until she finishes. Note one point to improve.

Check: She covered history and her area without stopping.

If needed: Nothing during. Everything goes to Stage 7.

Move on when: She has finished and stopped speaking.

Goal: To give one point from what she said, and retask only that part.

Run it: Name what worked in her words. One point. Write first and clearer version. Retask 20 to 40 seconds.

Check: The retask is shorter than the performance and contains the correction.

If needed: Shorten to a single sentence.

Move on when: She has said the corrected part once.

Optional: Ask where in the 31 August meeting this part appears.

Goal: To close on what she built and point at lesson 3 by what she will do.

Run it: Read the three lines. The next lesson is on 25 August — do not say tomorrow unless it is.

Check: She can say what she leaves with.

If needed: Ask for the one-sentence history once more, as the closing act.

Move on when: She has named one thing she can now do.

Goal: To connect to lesson 2 and set today’s limit: one example per category.

Run it: Ask for the one-sentence history from lesson 2. Then say today is four categories, one example each.

Check: She produced the one-sentence history.

If needed: Give her the first three words.

Move on when: She has said the history once.

Goal: To obtain her reading of the visitor’s interest.

Run it: Ask and wait. Diagnostic imaging is the expected answer — Carestream is imaging.

Check: She connects the visitor to a category.

If needed: Ask what Carestream sells.

Move on when: She has named a category.

Goal: To name the risk: the catalogue, and the number she must not improvise.

Run it: Read the three. The third is the one to mark: partner share is lesson 5 content, not today’s.

Check: She knows to forward the share question today.

If needed: Say the third risk again and give her the forwarding line.

Move on when: She has chosen one.

Goal: To obtain evidence of how she groups products.

Run it: Ask and stay quiet. Note whether she grouped or listed.

Check: You have a sample of her grouping.

If needed: If she freezes, say We work with four areas and wait.

Move on when: She has produced something.

Goal: To model the shape: category, then one example, then stop.

Run it: Read the four. Ask the question. The answer you want: one example is enough to place it.

Check: She sees that the example serves the category, not the other way round.

If needed: Ask which example she would use for imaging with this visitor.

Move on when: She has answered the question.

Goal: To fix five lines, including the one that protects her from a number.

Run it: Drill changing the category each time. Then ask a share question and require the fifth line.

Check: She uses the fifth line instead of guessing.

If needed: Cut to three lines and keep the fifth.

Move on when: She has said all five at least once.

Goal: To let her name partners without entering share numbers.

Run it: Ask the question. Then ask a share question and require the forwarding line.

Check: She names partners and forwards the share.

If needed: Give her the second line and let her build from it.

Move on when: She has said the Carestream line once, correctly.

Goal: To make the portfolio portable across listeners.

Run it: Three rounds. The category shape survives; only the example changes.

Check: The four categories survive all three rounds.

If needed: Drop to two listeners.

Move on when: She has presented for at least two listeners.

Goal: To run the whole lesson content once, with support.

Run it: One full run. Interrupt only after five seconds of silence.

Check: She goes from categories to partners without a gap.

If needed: Let her read the map.

Move on when: She has completed one run.

Goal: To obtain the main production: four categories with one example each, plus partners.

Run it: Ask and stay quiet until she finishes. Note one point.

Check: She covered the categories without turning it into a catalogue.

If needed: Nothing during.

Move on when: She has finished.

Goal: To give one point and retask only that part.

Run it: Name what worked. One point. First and clearer version. Retask 20 to 40 seconds.

Check: The retask contains the correction.

If needed: Shorten to one sentence.

Move on when: She has said the corrected part once.

Goal: To close and point at lesson 4 by what she will do.

Run it: Read the three lines. The next lesson is 26 August.

Check: She can say what she leaves with.

If needed: Ask for the four categories once more.

Move on when: She has named one thing she can now do.

Goal: To connect to lesson 3 and frame the two halves as ONE answer.

Run it: Ask for the four categories from lesson 3. Then say today is where and who keeps it working.

Check: She produced the categories.

If needed: Give her the first category.

Move on when: She has said the categories once.

Goal: To reframe coverage as a promise of support, not geography.

Run it: Ask the question from the buyer’s side. The answer you want names people, not cities.

Check: She answers with capability, not with a list of states.

If needed: Ask what she would want if she bought equipment for her own hospital.

Move on when: She has answered from the buyer’s side.

Goal: To name the specific risk: two blocks glued together instead of one answer.

Run it: Read the three. The first is the one that matters today.

Check: She sees that coverage plus service is one answer.

If needed: Say the bad version out loud in ten seconds: a list, then a list.

Move on when: She has chosen one.

Goal: To obtain evidence of whether she links the two halves on her own.

Run it: Ask the double question and stay quiet. Note if she answered both parts.

Check: You know whether she connects coverage to support.

If needed: If she freezes, say Our head office is in São Paulo and wait.

Move on when: She has produced something.

Goal: To show that the last line is what makes the first three matter.

Run it: Read the four. Ask the question. The answer is the fourth.

Check: She identifies the service line as the point.

If needed: Read the first three alone and ask what is missing.

Move on when: She has identified the fourth.

Goal: To fix five lines that answer where and who together.

Run it: Drill changing the region each time. Require the third line in every round.

Check: The service line appears in every version she produces.

If needed: Cut to three lines, keeping the third.

Move on when: She has said all five at least once.

Goal: To give one owned number and one clean refusal.

Run it: Ask the response-time question. Require the third line. The deck has no SLA and she must not invent one.

Check: She gives the number she has and forwards the one she does not.

If needed: Give her the third line and ask her to repeat it.

Move on when: She has forwarded the response time once.

Goal: To show that the same content answers three different questions.

Run it: Three rounds, one question each. The service line must appear in all three.

Check: The service line survives all three.

If needed: Two rounds is enough.

Move on when: She has answered at least two.

Goal: To run the full answer once, with support.

Run it: One run. Interrupt only after five seconds of silence.

Check: She connects the two halves without a gap.

If needed: Let her read the map.

Move on when: She has completed one run.

Goal: To obtain the main production against a real buying question.

Run it: Ask as the visitor and stay quiet. Note one point.

Check: She answered with coverage and service as one thing.

If needed: Nothing during.

Move on when: She has finished.

Goal: To give one point and retask only that part.

Run it: Name what worked. One point. First and clearer. Retask 20 to 40 seconds.

Check: The retask contains the correction.

If needed: Shorten to one sentence.

Move on when: She has said the corrected part once.

Goal: To close and point at lesson 5 by what she will do.

Run it: Read the three lines. The next lesson is 27 August.

Check: She can say what she leaves with.

If needed: Ask for the service line once more.

Move on when: She has named one thing she can now do.

Goal: To connect to lesson 4 and set the rule of the day: one sentence per chart.

Run it: Ask for the service line from lesson 4. Then state the rule: each chart gets one sentence, not a reading.

Check: She produced the service line.

If needed: Give her the first three words.

Move on when: She has said it once.

Goal: To separate reading a chart from summarising it.

Run it: Ask the question. The answer you want: it names the direction, not the digits.

Check: She distinguishes reading from meaning.

If needed: Read a row of numbers out loud and ask if that helped.

Move on when: She has answered the question.

Goal: To name the risk that is specific to numbers: the figure she does not have.

Run it: Read the three. The third is real: the deck has no recurring-revenue percentage. She must not create one.

Check: She knows that inventing a number is the worst outcome here.

If needed: Ask what she would say if she did not have the number.

Move on when: She has chosen one.

Goal: To obtain evidence of how she handles a number under a real question.

Run it: Ask and stay quiet. Note whether she read digits or gave a direction.

Check: You have a sample of her number-handling.

If needed: If she freezes, say Last year was and wait.

Move on when: She has produced something.

Goal: To model summarising: direction and comparison, digits available if asked.

Run it: Read the three. Ask the question. The answer: the exact figures, which stay on the slide.

Check: She sees that the digits live on the slide, not in her mouth.

If needed: Point at the slide and say the number is here.

Move on when: She has answered the question.

Goal: To fix five lines: three summaries, one redirection, one refusal.

Run it: Drill each. Then ask for recurring revenue and require the fifth line. Do this twice.

Check: She refuses cleanly instead of inventing.

If needed: Cut to two summaries and keep lines four and five.

Move on when: She has used the fifth line at least once without help.

Goal: To let her talk about the future without promising anything.

Run it: Ask the question. Then ask if the company will close the Midea deal, and require the third line.

Check: She marks the difference between plan and promise.

If needed: Say the third line for her and ask her to repeat it.

Move on when: She has used the third line once.

Goal: To rehearse the sequence that ends in a question she cannot answer.

Run it: Ask the three in order, without pausing between them. The third must produce the refusal line.

Check: She answers two and refuses the third without losing composure.

If needed: Ask only the first and third.

Move on when: She has refused the third cleanly.

Goal: To run the whole numbers block once, with support.

Run it: One run. Interrupt only after five seconds of silence.

Check: She moves through the charts without reading digits.

If needed: Let her read the map.

Move on when: She has completed one run.

Goal: To obtain the main production with the integrated Q&A of this lesson.

Run it: Ask, stay quiet, then ask two follow-ups — one answerable, one not. Note one point.

Check: She summarised, then handled both follow-ups.

If needed: Nothing during.

Move on when: She has finished both follow-ups.

Goal: To give one point and retask only that part.

Run it: Name what worked. One point. First and clearer. Retask 20 to 40 seconds.

Check: The retask contains the correction.

If needed: Shorten to one sentence.

Move on when: She has said the corrected part once.

Goal: To close and hand over to the simulation of lesson 6.

Run it: Read the three lines. The third is the handover — say that the next lesson is the full run.

Check: She knows the next lesson is the simulation.

If needed: Ask which part of the meeting she wants to run first on 28 August.

Move on when: She has named one thing she can now do.

Goal: To set the frame: integration, not new content.

Run it: Say it plainly: today nothing new is taught. Ask which part she wants to run first.

Check: She knows this is a run, not a lesson of new language.

If needed: Name the five blocks she already has.

Move on when: She has named where she wants to start.

Goal: To obtain her own priority for the run.

Run it: Ask and wait. Whatever she names gets the extra rehearsal in Stage 5.

Check: She named one part, not all of them.

If needed: Offer the five blocks and ask her to choose one.

Move on when: She has named one part.

Goal: To name the three failure modes she has language for.

Run it: Read the three. For each, ask which line she already has. She has all three.

Check: She maps each risk to a line she owns.

If needed: Point at the repair lines from lesson 1.

Move on when: She has matched at least two.

Goal: To obtain a first full-run sample before any adjustment.

Run it: Let her run for about two minutes without interrupting. Note where she slowed, not what was wrong.

Check: You have a sample of the whole arc.

If needed: If she stops, give the next block name only.

Move on when: She has run at least three blocks.

Goal: To make the order conscious, so she can recover it if interrupted.

Run it: Read the five. Ask the question — blocks three and four are the movable pair.

Check: She sees the order is a tool, not a script to memorise.

If needed: Ask which block must come first.

Move on when: She has answered the question.

Goal: To consolidate one line per lesson — nothing new.

Run it: Drill the five in sequence, then in reverse order. Reverse order proves they are not a memorised block.

Check: She produces all five in both orders.

If needed: Forward order only.

Move on when: She has said all five at least once.

Goal: To rehearse re-entry, which is the difference between a run and a meeting.

Run it: Interrupt her three times with different questions. Each time she answers or forwards, then returns.

Check: She returns to the block she left.

If needed: Interrupt once, and name the block she should return to.

Move on when: She has returned to her block at least twice.

Goal: To spend the extra rehearsal on her own priority, not yours.

Run it: Two rounds of the block she named in Stage 1. The second one shorter.

Check: The shorter version keeps the point.

If needed: One round is enough.

Move on when: She has run her chosen block twice.

Goal: To rehearse rapid-fire with a mix she can and cannot answer.

Run it: Ask the four without pausing. Two are answerable, two are forwards.

Check: She answers two and forwards two, without stopping.

If needed: Ask three.

Move on when: She has handled at least three.

Goal: To obtain the full simulation: the five blocks with two interruptions.

Run it: Let her run. Interrupt exactly twice, at natural points. Do not correct. Note one point.

Check: She ran the five blocks and recovered from both interruptions.

If needed: Interrupt once instead of twice.

Move on when: She has closed the meeting.

Goal: To leave her with one correction she can still absorb before 31 August.

Run it: Name what worked. Choose the point with most impact in the room, not the most frequent error. Retask 20 to 40 seconds.

Check: The retask is clean and she knows where it belongs on Monday.

If needed: Shorten to one sentence.

Move on when: She has said the corrected part once.

Goal: To close the cycle on what she can do, not on what is missing.

Run it: Read the three lines. Do not add new advice here — the last correction was Stage 7.

Check: She leaves naming something she can do.

If needed: Ask her to say the opening one last time.

Move on when: She has named one thing she can now do.
